content:
Apple will raise iPhone prices in Japan this month, with increases of up to 11%. Affected models include the iPhone 17 series, iPhone Air, and iPhone 16e. Below are the specific price hikes for each model and possible reasons behind the move.

The following are all models affected by this price increase, first spotted by iPhoneros:

Model Storage Old Price New Price Increase % Increase iPhone 17 Pro Max 256GB ¥194,800 ¥214,800 ¥20,000 10% iPhone 17 Pro 256GB ¥179,800 ¥194,800 ¥15,000 8% iPhone Air 256GB ¥159,800 ¥177,800 ¥18,000 11% iPhone 17e 256GB ¥99,800 ¥107,800 ¥8,000 8% iPhone 17 256GB ¥129,800 ¥142,800 ¥13,000 10% iPhone 16 128GB ¥114,800 ¥124,800 ¥10,000 9%

Apple did not explain why it raised iPhone prices in Japan, but it is likely related to currency fluctuations. The yen has recently fallen to its lowest level in 40 years, sitting at a historic weak point. The depreciation of the yen reduces Apple's dollar-denominated revenue from sales in Japan, so the company is likely using the price hike to bring iPhone pricing more in line with other markets.

Apple is facing pressure from rising component costs and raised prices on several products last month, including Mac and iPad. However, iPhone was not affected in the previous round of price hikes.

If this price increase in Japan is purely due to currency factors, other countries are unlikely to follow suit. Apple will hold its fiscal year 2025 third-quarter earnings call on July 30, during which management will provide further updates on product pricing.
